Reverse power is caused, not asserted: the rotor stays locked in step, so the board drives it round and real power flows in ([^1]). 400 kW shared, A draws 50.4 kW (lesson 6's example 10%), B carries 450.4 kW.

The lost field is derived from lesson 6's power = E V sin delta / Xs: 200 kW on 630 kVA = 0.32 pu, Xs 1.5; E 1.44 gives 19.3 deg; E 0.80 gives 36.5 deg and Q = (0.8 cos 36.5 - 1)/1.5 x 630 = -150 kVAr; past E = 0.48 no angle carries the kW, so the rotor slips ([^2]).

The decrement is computed from one rule: rated 630 000 / (1.732 x 440) = 826.7 A; first 826.7 / 0.15 = 5511 A; transient level 3307 A; PMG settles 3 x rated = 2480 A, 2636 A at 0.5 s; shunt 625 A at 0.5 s, below 2000 A near 0.15 s ([^3], [^4], [^6]). Steady current with the field held is E / Xs = 2.25 / 1.5 = 1.5 x rated, so 3 x needs forcing: the supply switch disproves the 300% myth by its cause.
